answer: In this PoA design, each identity is admitted only after completing a Wesolowski VDF: a prescribed chain of modular squarings whose dependencies force sequential evaluation. A claimant may ripple requests across a knoll or ridge of GPUs, but hardware cannot turn one chain into parallel work; simulating many clones therefore requires many full, time-bound chains. This physical bottleneck makes Sybil identities costly, while the compact proof enables fast verification.
